title: Sqrt(x)
interviewTips: Clarify truncation: return floor(sqrt(x)), e.g. x=8 returns 2, and confirm x is non-negative 32-bit int.
Trade-off: Binary Search is O(log x) and interview-safe with no overflow if you use division or long; Newton is faster in practice with quadratic convergence but needs convergence reasoning.
Edge-case tip: avoid overflow of mid*mid in C++/Java by using long or comparing mid <= x / mid, and handle x=0 and x=1 early.

approaches.name: Approach 1: Brute Force Linear Search
approaches.intuition: Squares are strictly increasing for non-negative numbers, so try candidates 1,2,3... until square exceeds x, then previous number is floor sqrt.
approaches.theory: We search smallest i with i*i > x. Correctness follows from monotonicity of f(i)=i*i. Use 64-bit for i*i to avoid 32-bit overflow. It checks about sqrt(x) values.

timeComplexity.explanation: Checks up to about sqrt(x)+1 candidates, each O(1). For x near 2^31-1 this is ~46340 iterations.

edgeCases: max int x=2147483647 returns 46340 without overflow using long

approaches.name: Approach 2: Binary Search on Answer
approaches.intuition: Answer lies in [0, x]. Since squaring is monotonic, we can binary search this range for largest mid with mid*mid <= x.
approaches.theory: Maintain invariant: answer in [left, right]. Let mid=(left+right)/2. If mid*mid <= x, answer >= mid so move left up and record ans; else answer < mid so move right down. Halves search space each step. Bound right to x//2 for x>=2 to halve steps. Use long or division to avoid overflow.

timeComplexity.explanation: Search space size ~x/2 halved each iteration, about 31 steps max for 32-bit int.

edgeCases: perfect square e.g. x=16 returns 4 via early equality
large x e.g. 2147483647 no overflow due to long

approaches.name: Approach 3: Newton Method (Newton-Raphson)
approaches.intuition: Solve r*r - x = 0 by iterative improvement: start from r=x and repeatedly average r with x/r to converge to sqrt.
approaches.theory: Newton update for f(r)=r*r-x is r = r - f(r)/fprime(r) = (r + x/r)/2. Sequence decreases monotonically to sqrt(x) when starting above it. Integer version r = (r + x/r)/2 with loop while r*r > x converges to floor sqrt. Quadratic convergence gives very few iterations.

timeComplexity.explanation: Quadratic convergence, typically <10 iterations for 32-bit range; often faster than binary search in practice.

edgeCases: x=0 returns 0 to avoid divide by zero
perfect square e.g. x=9 converges exactly to 3
large x uses long for r*r comparison
